clue.text: Cheer up, getting a drink before one's ritual departure

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for the cheer is read from bottom to top

parts.note: rah is a cheer, as in rah-rah
kir is a drink of white wine and blackcurrant liqueur
one is I, the Roman numeral, with 's as 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone toasts with a drink before a solemn ceremony of leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reads the cheer bottom to top; 'getting' and 'before' simply join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Hara-kiri is Japanese ritual suicide, a ceremonial way of leaving life.

clue.text: Language of Flanders evidently

indicators.note: of signals that the language is made of letters taken from the words that follow

explanation.surface: Apparently a tongue spoken in Flanders, the Belgian region.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across flandERS Evidently; 'evidently' pretends to vouch for the claim but is part of the hiding place.
explanation.definitionFit: Erse is an old name for Scottish or Irish Gaelic, a language.

clue.text: Hot shot lost points

indicators.note: shot in the sense of ruined or knocked about, so the letters that follow are jumbled

parts.note: N and E are compass points, north and east

explanation.surface: A sharpshooter, feeling the heat, has dropped points in a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' looks like part of 'Hot shot', but it is the anagram signal on LOST plus NE.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot is slang for stolen goods, recently taken and risky to sell.

clue.text: Dig a road? You don't say!

parts.note: to dig is slang for to understand, to get
a road is a way

explanation.surface: Someone is incredulous at a suggestion to dig up a road.
explanation.definitionFit: Get away! is an exclamation of disbelief, just like 'You don't say!'.

clue.text: Writing about the end — or lament for the dead

indicators.note: the words are written out again in a rearranged order, so their letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Composing something about the end of life, or a song of mourning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writing about' is the anagram signal on THE END OR; the dash merely separates the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A threnode, a variant of threnody, is a song or poem of mourning.

clue.text: Darling bow set off ceremonial garb

indicators.note: set off in the sense of arranged differently or sent away from its place, signalling a mixing

explanation.surface: A lovely bow shows off formal wedding attire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set off' reads as 'enhance', but it signals the anagram of DARLING BOW.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedding dress is the formal costume worn by a bride at the ceremony.

clue.text: Cyclist taking small car to King's Cross?

parts.note: Merc is short for Mercedes, a car; small signals the shortening
KX is the abbreviation for King's Cross, the London station

explanation.surface: A cyclist hitches a lift in a little car to a London station.
explanation.walkthrough: Eddy Merckx is the great Belgian racing cyclist; 'small' means the car name is cut short, not that the car is little.
explanation.definitionFit: Eddy Merckx won the Tour de France five times, a celebrated Belgian racing cyclist.

clue.text: Surrealist exhibiting coarse sandstone framed by friend

indicators.note: framed by means the sandstone word sits inside the friend word like a picture in a frame

parts.note: a mate is a friend
grit is a coarse-grained sandstone, gritstone

explanation.surface: A surrealist painting depicts rough rock set in a frame from a pal.
explanation.walkthrough: René Magritte was a Belgian surrealist painter, which suits 'framed'.
explanation.definitionFit: René Magritte was a leading Belgian painter of the surrealist movement.

clue.text: Creator of 12? Gent has no books by her

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: has no means the word gent loses the letters for the books

parts.note: NT, the New Testament, is a collection of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A man without his reading matter is beside a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 is the comic-strip boy reporter's entry; 'by' means beside, so the woman's word sits next to the trimmed gent.
explanation.definitionFit: Hergé, the Belgian cartoonist, wrote and drew the comic adventures of the boy reporter at 12.

clue.text: As shown by setter, foremost characters in Flanders achieve renown

indicators.note: foremost characters means the first letter of each of the next words

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves as me

explanation.surface: The setter claims that leading people in Flanders become celebrated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As shown by' is a loose link joining the setter's ME to FA; some solvers felt the order was unsignalled.
explanation.definitionFit: Fame and renown are synonyms for wide celebrity and reputation.

clue.text: Crooked play with these? Lots of actors initially decided otherwise

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of each of the three words
otherwise means arranged in another way, so the letters of decided are rearranged

explanation.surface: Many performers had a different decision about a dishonest game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crooked play' reads as a dishonest game; 'otherwise' rearranges the letters of 'decided' after the three initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Loaded dice are weighted to land a certain way, the tools of a cheat at gambling.

clue.text: Colour in character in picture books

parts.note: a tint is a colour or shade
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone colours in a figure in an illustrated book.
explanation.walkthrough: Tintin is the boy reporter of the Belgian comic albums.
explanation.definitionFit: Tintin is the young reporter hero of Hergé's comic albums for children.

clue.text: Awful monster due for reform

indicators.note: reform means to form again in a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dreadful beast is overdue for rehabilitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link; 'reform' signals the anagram of MONSTER DUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tremendous originally meant fearful or dreadful, so awful in its root sense.

clue.text: Fit man embraces father on the Fourth of July

indicators.note: embraces means the man's name holds the father word inside it

parts.note: Alex is a man's name
pop is an informal word for father

indicators.note: the fourth of points to the fourth letter of the word July

explanation.surface: A healthy man hugs his dad on Independence Day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fit' looks like an adjective for the man but is the noun definition; 'the Fourth of July' is not the holiday but letter four, Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Apoplexy is a stroke or seizure, a sudden fit.

clue.text: He wrote in French — outwardly a simple chap

indicators.note: outwardly means the chap's name is on the outside, around the other piece

parts.note: Simple Simon is the nursery-rhyme simpleton
en is French for in

explanation.surface: A naive writer appeared to compose in French.
explanation.walkthrough: Georges Simenon, creator of Maigret, was a Belgian who wrote in French; 'He wrote' is the definition and 'in French' gives EN.
explanation.definitionFit: Georges Simenon was a prolific Belgian novelist, author of the Maigret stories.

clue.text: One has butcher's shop assistant? First job not started

indicators.note: not started means the word job loses its first letter

parts.note: a server is someone who serves in a shop

explanation.surface: A butcher's shop assistant, whose first job was never begun.
explanation.walkthrough: Butcher's is rhyming slang: butcher's hook = look, so one who has a look is an onlooker. 'First' puts the trimmed job before the assistant.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a butcher's means having a look, so someone taking a look is a watcher.

clue.text: Soldiers distrust defensive position

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are British Army soldiers
doubt means distrust

explanation.surface: Troops are wary of a fortified post.
explanation.definitionFit: A redoubt is a small fortification, a stronghold for defence.

clue.text: Arabs given gold to replace eastern king

indicators.note: to replace means the gold letters take the place of the eastern letter

parts.note: Bedouin are nomadic Arabs of the desert
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Desert Arabs are handed gold to put in place of an oriental monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' is a link; Baudouin was King of the Belgians from 1951 to 1993.
explanation.definitionFit: Baudouin was the Belgian monarch for over forty years.

clue.text: Leader in priesthood, say

indicators.note: leader in means the first letter of the word priesthood

parts.note: to relate is to say or tell

explanation.surface: A head of the clergy, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like 'for example' but gives RELATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A prelate is a senior churchman such as a bishop, a leader of the clergy.

clue.text: Conciliator one might hear in a city in Italy?

indicators.note: one might hear means the word is identified by how it is spoken

parts.note: a Pisa: Pisa is a city in Italy

explanation.surface: A peacemaker one might listen to in an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent, 'a Pisa' and the answer sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: An appeaser makes concessions to placate others, as a conciliator does.

clue.text: Detective raising cap outside city

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising means the whole assembled piece is read upwards
outside means the cap word wraps around the city

parts.note: top means a cap or lid
Rio de Janeiro, often just Rio, is a city

explanation.surface: A detective lifts his hat outside a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising' reverses the whole cap-round-city piece, not the cap alone; Hercule Poirot is Agatha Christie's Belgian detective.
explanation.definitionFit: Hercule Poirot is Agatha Christie's famous Belgian private detective.

clue.text: Spread for supporter debarred

parts.note: a fan is a supporter
debarred, shut out, means out

explanation.surface: A supporter is banned from the ground and spreads out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To fan out is to spread outwards in a wide arc.

clue.text: Composer caught in open

indicators.note: in means the caught letter goes inside the open word

parts.note: frank means open or candid
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A composer was caught out in the open.
explanation.walkthrough: César Franck was a Belgian-born composer.
explanation.definitionFit: César Franck was a Belgian-born composer and organist of the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Maid of all work recalled in play

indicators.note: in play means the letters are moving about freely, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drudge of a servant is remembered in a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled in play' looks like a memory of a theatre role; the anagram signal is 'play' acting on RECALLED IN. The pantomime heroine fits the surface too.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinderella is the fairy-tale drudge made to do all the household work.

clue.text: Dry piece of writing on Belgian capital's destiny

indicators.note: capital means the first letter, the head, of the word Belgian

parts.note: lot means one's destiny or fate

explanation.surface: A dull document about the fate of Belgium's capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Belgian capital' tempts one toward Brussels, but it means the letter B. 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To blot is to dry wet ink on a page with blotting paper.

clue.text: Singer with two couples from Brussels?

indicators.note: two couples from means two pairs of adjacent letters are taken from the word Brussels

explanation.surface: A singer accompanied by two pairs of people from Belgium's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The two pairs are BR and EL in BRusSELs, leaving out the other letters; Jacques Brel was a Belgian singer-songwriter.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacques Brel was a celebrated Belgian singer-songwriter of chanson.

clue.text: Old blend may be advantageous

parts.note: to fuse is to blend or merge

explanation.surface: A traditional mix might bring benefits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' is a link between the wordplay and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of use is helpful, beneficial, advantageous.

clue.text: Ate abed?

definitions.meaning: settled snugly in bed with the covers

explanation.definitionFit: Tucking in means eating heartily, and being tucked in means snug under the bedclothes.
